challenge.title: Fix the Frontend
challenge.description: Clicking Increase should add 2, but the counter only goes up by 1.
challenge.initialTerminal:
[Example failure output — not an executed test]
$ npm test
FAIL src/Counter.test.tsx
  ✕ counter should increase by 2
  Expected: 2
  Received: 1

Hint: React state updates can use a stale value.
Tests: 1 failed, 0 passed
challenge.hint: Try setCount(count + 2), or two functional updater calls.

review.task: Clicking Increase should add 2, but the counter only goes up by 1. increment() calls setCount(count + 1) twice, and both calls read the same old value.
review.expected: Clicking Increase once raises the count by exactly 2 (0 -> 2 -> 4).
criteria: One click of Increase raises count by exactly 2.
Accepted approaches include setCount(count + 2) or two functional updates such as setCount(c => c + 1).
The component still renders the count and the Increase button.

challenge.title: Fix the Backend
challenge.description: Orders must not reduce stock below zero.
challenge.initialTerminal:
[Example failure output — not an executed test]
$ npm test
FAIL inventory.test.js
  ✕ rejects a purchase larger than stock
  Expected: order rejected
  Received: -3

Hint: Validate the requested quantity before subtracting.
Tests: 1 failed, 0 passed
challenge.hint: Add an if statement that rejects quantity > stock.

review.task: Orders must not reduce stock below zero. purchase() subtracts quantity from stock without checking it first.
review.expected: If quantity is greater than stock, the order is rejected (return early or throw). Otherwise it returns stock - quantity. Buying exactly the remaining stock is allowed and leaves 0.
criteria: An order with quantity greater than stock is rejected by returning early or throwing an error.
The check actually runs before the subtraction; an empty or unreachable check does not count.
Valid orders (quantity <= stock) still return stock - quantity.

challenge.title: Fix the Deployment
challenge.description: The backend listens on port 8080, but the reverse proxy is misconfigured.
challenge.initialTerminal:
[Example failure output — not an executed test]
$ curl /api/health
502 Bad Gateway
  connect() failed (111: Connection refused)
  Upstream port: 3000
  Backend port: 8080

Hint: Check the proxy_pass port.
Tests: 1 failed, 0 passed

review.task: The backend listens on port 8080, but the reverse proxy sends /api/ traffic to port 3000, causing 502 Bad Gateway.
review.expected: Requests to /api/ are forwarded to http://localhost:8080.
criteria: The /api/ location proxies to http://localhost:8080 with valid nginx syntax (including the semicolon).
No active proxy_pass to port 3000 remains.
Lines commented out with # do not count.
